Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 18-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Digital design verifications [ECE_4407]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Write the test bench program of NAND-NOR logic in System Verilog with set of Test inputs and             (5)  
  expected outputs as shown in the Figure below.  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Explain the working of a Full Adder using its truth table and logic diagram and write the                (3)  
  corresponding Verilog code.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           Explain the importance of a Verification Plan (V-Plan).                                                  (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Remember"  
  
2)                Analyze different types of verification, its goals, and various verification methodologies, explaining   (5)  
  how they interrelate to ensure a reliable VLSI design.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Compute and contrast between Verilog, VHDL and System Verilog with a programming example of (3)  
  HALF adder.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           Explain any two advantages of logic verification in the digital design process.                          (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3)                Discuss the challenges in logic verification at lower technology nodes (e.g., 5 nm) with example and (5)  
  suggest strategies to overcome them.  
  Page #1

A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)          Apply the concept of functional coverage to a System Verilog verification environment and explain         (3)  
  the way it measures the completeness of test scenarios in a design verification process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)          Design a simple testbench for an AND gate and explain its components.                                     (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)               Apply UVM and explain block diagram of a UVM environment to verify an ALU (Arithmetic Logic               (5)  
  Unit).  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)          Apply the concept of digital design verification to explain how it ensures correctness and reliability    (3)  
  within the VLSI design flow, using suitable examples from practical design scenarios.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)          Explain the role of Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) in modern verification environments          (2)  
  and how it improves the verification process.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5)               Analyze how a race condition can occur in a simulation testbench and describe the methods and             (5)  
  tools you would use to detect and debug it.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)          Discuss the steps to compile, elaborate, and simulate a design in Verilog.                                (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)          Explain the need for Synthesis in VLSI design.                                                            (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"
